parameters.query:
-- PERS-001/002: one immutable row per feedback event.
--
-- Parameterized, not interpolated. The previous version built this
-- statement by pasting `JSON.stringify($json)` between quotes, which
-- is a SQL injection through any field a user can influence -- and
-- would have broken on something as ordinary as an apostrophe in a
-- track title long before anyone attacked it.
--
-- PERS-002 deduplication: the idempotency key WF-001 already
-- requires for this intent is what makes a double-click one event
-- rather than two. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a retried request is
-- harmless and the row that exists is the one that stays -- events
-- are immutable, so the first write wins by definition.
INSERT INTO feedback_events (event_type, user_id, guest_session_id, context)
SELECT $1, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4::jsonb
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM feedback_events
  WHERE context->>'idempotency_key' = $5
)
RETURNING id::text;

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ request_id: $('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.request_id, user_id: $('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.user_id, guest_id: ($('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.envelope?.identity?.guest_id || null), idempotency_key: $('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.idempotency_key, signals: Object.assign({}, ($('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.envelope?.body?.feedback || {}), { discovery_mode: ($('When Executed by Another Workflow').item.json.envelope?.body?.recommendation_context?.discovery_mode || null) }) }) }}
